comment: The read catalogue and its decode vectors. Every binding with a chain client must expose exactly these (facade, method) reads, plus `pin_method` on each façade that has one. A case is a transcript: `exchanges` lists every JSON-RPC request the read makes, in order, each with the node's `result` (which may be null) or the `error` it refused with. A `pinnable` read is recorded pinned at `at`; unpinned it first asks for the finalized head, which is `at`, and then makes the same requests. A read that is not pinnable makes the same requests either way, and so does a case that fails with no exchanges: it is refused before the chain is asked anything. The read must make exactly those requests and then either return `expected` (the JSON value) serialized as exactly `expected_json` (the canonical bytes: no whitespace, fields in declared order, only quotes, backslashes and control characters escaped; `null` for a `nullable` read with nothing to return), or fail with a chain error naming `error.target`. `args` are what a caller passes, by the row's argument names; argument types are account, string, u32, u64, u128, hash, bytes, page and call_args (a call's arguments as an ordered list of {name, type, value}, which each binding turns into the form its `tx` takes). A case with a `client` is read by a client that would sign as `client.signer`, for the member `client.principal` if any; any other case by a read-only one. `shape` names each field's form: address (SS58), u32 (number), u64/u128 (decimal string), text (string, or {hex} when not UTF-8), hex, bool, string, A|B|C (one variant name); `?` marks a field that may be null, and {"?": shape} an object that may be. Raw bytes are bare hex except inside exchanges and results, which are verbatim. Method names are snake_case here; bindings apply their own convention.
